A1.justification: Both complete, readable 20-page PDFs describe the same research, renamed from StageVAR to FasterVAR. Text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable matching despite extensive layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original Infinity/STAR acceleration experiments, GenEval/DPG and COCO results, ablations, rank statistics, and a user study involving 69 participants and 42 image pairs.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and appendix analyses, including the relocated user study, and adds HPSv2.1 and PickScore results in Table 5.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 and Algorithm 1 retain early-stage preservation, late-stage CFG removal, predetermined ranks, random projection, and representative token restoration. FasterVAR is a rename; expanded restoration explanations and Figure 8 describe existing procedures.

E1.justification: Reported coverage remains GenEval, DPG, COCO2014/2017, complex and rare prompts, and diverse aspect ratios. v2 introduces HPSv2.1 and PickScore as evaluation metrics without identifying an additional dataset or distinct test scenario.

E2.justification: Table 3 retains the same comparison methods, including FastVAR and SkipVAR. The new preference-score table evaluates already established vanilla-versus-accelerated Infinity and STAR comparisons; it introduces no new comparator.

E3.justification: v2 adds HPSv2.1 and PickScore evaluation in Table 5. Existing model sizes, generation settings, COCO sample counts, and user-study procedures remain unchanged. The prompt set and sampling protocol for the new preference scores are not specified.

E4.justification: The rank and CFG ablations, random-projection robustness, frequency analysis, complex-prompt examples, and STAR analyses are retained. The quality–latency comparison moves to Appendix D.2. New Figure 8 explains existing strategies rather than adding an experimental analysis.

E5.justification: Appendix A.1 retains the same sampling information and rank means and standard deviations in Tables 7–9. v2 adds no repeated-run disclosures, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates for the new preference scores.

E6.justification: New Table 5 reports HPSv2.1/PickScore values: Infinity 30.48/23.12 versus accelerated 30.07/23.00, and STAR 29.16/21.56 versus accelerated 29.06/21.28. These are additional results, not improvements over v1. Retained quantitative results match; the rank montage drops the book-image example series while retaining the teddy-bear series.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8, the energy-based rank definition, row-sampling assumption, and cached restoration approximations remain unchanged. Figure 8 makes existing operations explicit but introduces no substantive mathematical definition, theorem, proof, or derivation.

C1.justification: Both versions claim training-free, stage-selective acceleration exploiting semantic irrelevance and low-rank features, reaching 3.4× speedup with negligible quality loss. v2 replaces explicit abstract score drops with 'almost no performance loss,' but retains the original 0.01/0.26 figures in the introduction.

C2.justification: Interpretations of stage formation, the intermediate-rank optimum, prompt robustness, and STAR applicability remain unchanged. New preference scores reinforce the existing quality-preservation interpretation. Replacing the general societal-impact caveats does not change a substantive mechanism explanation or applicability limitation.

D1.justification: Appendix E newly supplies exact prompts for numerous illustrated results, beyond the complex prompts already disclosed in both versions. v2 removes the explicit promise to release all source code and scripts after review while retaining a renamed code link. Hardware and acceleration settings remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Faster Diffusion, HPSv2, and Pick-a-Pic and removes SwiftBrushv2. Other changes largely update bibliographic metadata. The positioning relative to existing VAR acceleration methods remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The method and title are renamed, selected passages are edited, and restoration explanations are expanded. Experimental subsections are consolidated, two analyses move to Appendix D, and strategy and prompt sections are added. Acknowledgments and a brief impact statement replace earlier statement material; most scientific prose is retained.

P2.justification: The main text changes from single-column to two-column presentation, extensively resizing and relocating displays. v2 adds Table 5 and a full-page strategy diagram, relocates the user-study and latency plots to the appendix, and rearranges the rank and aspect-ratio montages.

improvement.justification: The added preference scores, clearer restoration explanation and Figure 8, and exact illustration prompts modestly improve empirical support, clarity, and reproducibility. Existing results remain intact. The new metric protocol is underspecified, and removing explicit release, ethics, and LLM-use statements reduces transparency, but these costs do not outweigh the concrete documentation gains.
